statement: The system shall support creating and maintaining shared terms and data definitions.
The system shall support publishing reusable XML structures and schemas that other applications can reference.
The system shall allow users and authorized applications to create XML documents from XML schemas.
The system shall allow users and authorized applications to consume incoming XML documents.
The system shall allow users and authorized applications to query or retrieve shared definitions and documents as needed.
The system shall allow applications to access distributed data through logical XML objects or views instead of requiring knowledge of the underlying physical database.
The system shall provide basic update and management functions for distributed data.
The system shall preserve the normal defense classification handling already in place for XML services.
Data stored or exposed through the XML layer shall carry the correct classification and shall be accessible only to users or applications with matching authorization.
The XML services shall enforce classification consistently on terms, schemas, documents, and views.
Older schema versions shall remain available.
Schema changes shall be managed so existing consumers do not break unexpectedly.
Breaking schema changes shall require a new version and explicit migration or coordination.
Authorized users and applications shall be able to update distributed data through logical XML representations when a view is defined as updatable.
The system shall distinguish between read-only access, query access, and controlled update access for XML views.
Controlled update access for XML views shall be based on policy and the specific data source.
A logical XML view shall be updatable only when the underlying data can be mapped back to a single authoritative source or to a clearly defined set of sources without ambiguity.
A logical XML view that joins multiple sources, aggregates data, or contains derived values shall be read-only unless a safe update path is explicitly defined.

Updates through a logical XML view shall be limited to authorized users or applications that have both the required security clearance and the required business permission for that specific view or data domain.
The system shall validate the XML against the schema and any business rules before accepting an update.
The system shall detect update conflicts by checking whether the underlying data has changed since it was read, using version or timestamp control.
If an update conflict occurs, the system shall reject the update and return a clear error so the caller can reread and resubmit.
Successful updates shall propagate back to the source system or database in a controlled way.
If a write fails partway through propagation, the service shall roll back the update or leave the data in a known consistent state.
The interview scope includes clarifying common XML services needs for the DII operating environment.
The interview scope includes clarifying reusable schemas for the DII operating environment.
The interview scope includes clarifying XML document handling for the DII operating environment.
The interview scope includes clarifying vendor-independent data access for the DII operating environment.
The solution shall work for defense applications.
The solution shall support defense applications that need to share structured data consistently across different systems and databases.
Different programs shall define their own schemas and data terms.
When programs need to exchange information, they shall use point-to-point integrations or local database interfaces that do not always line up well.
The system shall support reuse to avoid difficulty and duplication when a new application needs the same data structure or access pattern.
Applications shall not each invent their own XML structures and access methods.
The system shall provide a common service for authorized users to register shared terms.
The system shall allow users to create XML documents in a consistent way.
Applications shall access distributed information without being tied to one vendor’s database technology.
Only authorized users and applications shall be able to use the core capabilities.
The system shall allow users to find existing shared terms and reusable schemas before creating something new.
The system shall provide solid version control and governance for shared terms and schemas.
The system shall validate XML documents against the registered schemas before they are exchanged or stored.
Schema reuse and discovery shall be delivered first.
An authorized user shall be able to search for existing schemas by name, purpose, domain, or related terms.
An authorized user shall be able to inspect enough detail about a schema to decide whether it can be reused as-is or extended.
If no suitable schema exists, the user shall be able to know what schemas are available so they can build something compatible rather than starting from scratch.
When a user needs a new XML structure, the system shall allow the user to search the repository for an existing schema.
The system shall help prevent multiple versions of the same concept.
The system shall make different systems easier to integrate.
Access to schema details should be limited to authorized users and applications.
An authorized user shall be able to see the full schema definition when reviewing a schema.
The system shall provide summaries for quick browsing of schemas.
Application owners and data stewards should be considered valuable sources of input because they understand what consuming systems need and which terms must remain consistent.
Security and accreditation personnel should be involved because the solution concerns authorized access and shared data in a defense environment.
People who operate the underlying infrastructure should be involved because the vendor-independent access capability must fit how distributed data is actually managed.
The system shall enable authorized teams to find XML schemas and shared terms quickly enough to avoid reinventing them for each application.
The system shall allow users to manage XML content through the common services.
The system shall support less duplication when users manage and consume XML content through the common services.
Governance needs to be practical.
The control over updates to shared terms and schemas should not be so heavy that people avoid using the service.
Mission and support applications shall not handle XML and shared data structures in inconsistent, application-specific ways.
The DII operating environment shall provide a common service for authorized users and applications to share terms.
The common service shall allow sharing of terms, schemas, and XML documents without depending on a specific database or vendor product.
The common service shall make data exchange more standardized, reusable, and easier to maintain across different systems.
The system shall enforce access controls so that only authorized users and systems can use shared content.
The system shall be reliable enough for operational use.
The system shall be responsive enough to avoid becoming a bottleneck for applications exchanging data.
The system shall reduce integration time.
The system shall reduce data exchange errors.
The system shall reduce maintenance effort over time.
The system shall lower the cost of connecting systems.
The system shall improve interoperability.
The primary users of the XML services shall be application developers and system integrators.
Data stewards or content owners shall register approved terms and structures.
Administrators shall manage access and governance for the XML services.
End users shall not directly interact with the service.
End users shall benefit indirectly from improved system interoperability and more consistent data exchange.
Developers and integrators use the system during design, build, and maintenance work.
The system must support keeping definitions consistent across programs.
Domain terminology shall be defined centrally by the data steward or owning organization.
Each domain term shall have a clear definition.
Each domain term shall have a controlled name.
Each domain term shall include whatever structure is needed to reuse it consistently across programs.
Disputes about meaning or versioning shall go through the governance process.
Schemas and reusable definitions shall have lifecycle states.
During draft or review, the content shall be editable.
Once approved and active, the content shall be protected from uncontrolled changes.
In pending approval state, the system shall allow reviewers to comment and approve the content.
The system shall capture the disputed term or schema version.
The XML services shall support the metadata requirements imposed by applicable policies.
The system shall preserve version history.
The system shall prevent unauthorized overwrites.
The system shall enforce retention or deprecation rules so users do not accidentally rely on content that is no longer approved.
Users shall be able to search.
Users shall be able to compare versions.
Users shall be able to see relationships between a schema, its terms, and the documents that depend on it without having to dig through technical detail.
The system shall provide simple guardrails to prevent common mistakes.
The system shall prompt users when they are about to use a deprecated version.
The XML services shall handle a growing number of schemas, terms, and XML documents without performance degradation as more programs come on board.
The XML services shall provide high availability so that mission applications can rely on them during normal operations.
The XML services shall support concurrent users and automated application calls.
The XML services shall provide graceful degradation or clear recovery behavior if a backend store or network segment is unavailable.
The system shall have its initial capacity verified with the programs that will actually use the service.
The system shall start with a moderate catalog of shared terms and schemas.
The system shall support significant growth as more mission and support applications adopt it and publish their own structures.
The system shall be able to handle peak usage when multiple applications register or validate documents at the same time.
The system shall be planned to handle bursts in both human access and machine-to-machine calls.
Under peak load, noncritical write or publishing actions may queue briefly.
If a component fails, the system shall keep core registry functions available where possible.
If a component fails, the system shall fail cleanly rather than returning corrupted or partial content.
The system shall avoid becoming a single point of failure for mission applications.
The system shall provide clear error reporting.
The system shall support recovery after an outage.
The system shall provide strong monitoring.
The system shall provide alerting.
The system shall automatically retry transient failures.
The system shall support fallback strategies.
The system shall clearly mark cached content so that it is not mistaken for the authoritative source.
The system shall provide rapid detection and recovery to support mission continuity.
The system shall support keyboard navigation.
The system shall be compatible with screen readers.
The system shall provide readable contrast.
The system shall not rely on color alone to convey status.
The system shall work in constrained environments.
The system shall support users on older workstations.
The system shall support users on secure networks.
The system shall support users on lower-bandwidth connections.
The XML service shall support approved screen readers on locked-down defense desktops.
The XML service shall support browsers that are not always current.
The XML service shall support remote or disconnected use.
The XML service shall remain usable when bandwidth is limited.
The XML service shall remain usable when large XML structures are hard to load or navigate.
The XML service shall not require extra plugins.
The XML service shall not require specialized client software.
The system shall provide accessible search and filtering.
The system shall provide clear hierarchical navigation for schemas and document structures.
The system shall expose status messages to assistive technologies in a way that is easy to understand.
The system shall expose validation errors to assistive technologies in a way that is easy to understand.
The system shall expose change notifications to assistive technologies in a way that is easy to understand.
The system shall offer text-based views and downloadable formats that preserve structure so users can inspect content without depending on a rich client.
The system shall support accredited legacy desktops with limited browser support.
The system shall work with approved assistive tools such as screen readers and magnifiers that vary by site.
The system shall accommodate users working in secure or disconnected environments where software updates are slow.
The service shall not depend on the newest web features.
The service shall not depend on frequent client-side changes.
The system shall provide simple navigation.
The system shall provide predictable layouts.
The system shall have low dependency on local plugins.
The service shall allow gradual improvements to the interface and accessibility features while keeping older clients functioning.
The service shall support modular updates.
The service shall have good documentation.
Migration to the new XML services shall be phased.
The most critical and most reused schemas shall be migrated first.
Migration shall not attempt to convert everything at once.
The migration process shall account for schema differences.
The migration process shall account for inconsistent naming or structure across programs.
Older documents shall still validate or be transformable cleanly during migration.
The migration approach shall provide mapping guidance.
The migration approach shall provide transformation support.
The migration approach shall include a parallel run period so teams can verify the new service before full cutover.
The system shall be used whenever different mission or support applications need to share structured data without each application inventing its own format or database interface.
The system shall support registering common terms.
The system shall support pulling information from distributed sources in a consistent way.
The system shall avoid tight coupling to any one vendor’s database or storage implementation.
The service shall fit inside the Defense Information Infrastructure common operating environment.
The system shall comply with defense acquisition and hosting constraints.
The system shall complete required security accreditation steps.
The system shall follow procurement rules for the environment.
The system shall remain available when a remote source is temporarily unreachable, a network link is down, or one consuming application is disrupted while others still need access to shared data.
The system shall define which data and transactions must remain available during interruptions and what delay or fallback behavior is acceptable.
The system's basic lookup and retrieval functions shall feel near immediate for day-to-day use.
Registering new terms, schemas, or structures may tolerate a short wait during day-to-day use.
The system shall treat the source of truth and data freshness carefully.
The system shall return a XML document that matches the registered definition exactly when exact matching is required.
The system shall support partial matches only for search or discovery.
The system shall provide complete and validated results for actual exchange and processing.
When discrepancies exist between sources, the system shall favor the authoritative registered definition or the approved data source.
The exact conflict-resolution rule for discrepancies between sources shall be defined.
Authorized users and applications should be able to register, define, create, and use XML assets.
Not everyone should have the same level of access to XML assets.
The people who register terms, define reusable schemas, or publish shared structures should be a smaller controlled group.
More users and consuming applications should be able to create and use XML documents based on approved definitions.
Access should be driven by mission role, need to know, security clearance or authorization level, and whether the requester is an approved system or a human operator.
The system shall require the authoritative registered definition for XML used in official exchange, reporting, or integration with other systems.
The system shall allow a local or alternate XML version only for internal drafting, testing, or isolated use that does not affect shared data.
The system shall restrict discovery and reuse to content the user or application is authorized to see.
The system shall route updates to a registered definition through the same controlled review and approval process as the original registration.
Discovery or reuse should be further limited when a definition is still in draft.
Discovery or reuse should be further limited when a definition has export or distribution restrictions.
Discovery or reuse should be further limited when a definition is tied to a sensitive mission area where only a subset of users should know it exists.
Reuse may be limited if a schema is marked for a particular program or enclave and has not been approved for broader use.
If someone requests an update without approval, the system should not let them modify the registered version directly.
If someone requests an update without approval, the system should either reject the change with a clear message or route it into a review workflow, depending on how the governance process is set up.
The system shall manage shared terms or vocabularies as main entities.
The system shall manage reusable XML schemas or structures as main entities.
The system shall manage XML documents or messages built from the reusable XML schemas or structures as main entities.
The system shall manage metadata for the managed items.
The system shall manage version metadata for the managed items.
The system shall manage ownership metadata for the managed items.
The system shall manage status metadata for the managed items.
The system shall manage the approved source metadata for the managed items.
Analysts and data stewards shall define the shared structures.
Analysts and data stewards shall maintain the shared structures.
Applications shall consume the shared structures to create mission data consistently across systems.
Applications shall consume the shared structures to validate mission data consistently across systems.
Applications shall consume the shared structures to exchange mission data consistently across systems.
Applications shall consume the shared structures to retrieve mission data consistently across systems.
When an entity is drafted, its version should clearly mark it as preliminary.
When an entity is drafted, its owner should be identified.
When an entity is drafted, its status should indicate that it is not yet authoritative.
Once an entity is approved, the metadata should show who approved it.
Once an entity is approved, the metadata should show the current active version.
Once an entity is approved, the metadata should identify the authoritative source.
If an item is retired or superseded, its status should change so users and applications know not to use it for new exchange.
If an item is retired or superseded, it may still need to remain retrievable for legacy reference.
If metadata conflicts or is missing, the system should fail safe.
If metadata conflicts or is missing, the system should block promotion to approved status rather than guessing.
If metadata conflicts or is missing, the system should flag the item for manual review rather than guessing.
The system shall preserve existing systems' ability to exchange data without disruption, especially for mission-critical systems that depend on current repositories or message formats.
The system shall preserve legacy access to older definitions and documents so teams can support historical data and interfaces during the transition.
Users shall be able to find the correct approved definition.
The transition shall minimize manual rework and downtime.
The transition shall improve control and interoperability without breaking what is already in operational use.
The system shall keep content only as retained historical reference when it is too ambiguous or not needed for ongoing business use.
The system shall use operational value, conversion risk, and the ability to govern and reuse content without introducing errors or inconsistency as deciding factors.
The system shall not use shared XML services for temporary exchanges.
The system shall not use shared XML services for highly experimental exchanges.
The system shall determine handling of a data item based on whether it has ongoing enterprise value and can be governed safely.
If a data item is useful more broadly but contains sensitive details, it shall be masked or summarized before publication.
The system shall use the test of whether exposing a data item would add mission value without creating unnecessary risk or operational burden.
The system shall mark the revised version as pending review until it is approved.
If an asset is retired, the system shall clearly mark it as deprecated and provide guidance on the replacement if one exists.
The service rollout shall use a phased rollout rather than a big-bang release.
The rollout shall start with a limited pilot for a small set of trusted users and systems.
The rollout shall expand to additional programs only after the core registration, approval, and exchange functions are stable.
A staged deployment is the safest approach for this environment.
The schemas and terms shall evolve gradually as missions change and new data needs arise.
Existing definitions shall be refined for clarity or interoperability.
Interfaces shall be able to expand.
Interface expansion shall be backward-compatible so current consumers can keep working while they adopt the new version.
Changes shall be introduced through versioned releases.
Changes shall be introduced with advance notice.
Changes shall be introduced with clear migration guidance.
Changes shall include a deprecation period before anything old is removed.
Existing users shall not be forced into an immediate change.
Systems shall have time to adjust on their own schedule.
Different defense applications shall not manage their XML definitions, terms, and data exchanges independently, because that approach causes duplication, inconsistency, and extra integration work.
The service shall provide a single controlled place for users to register shared structures.
The service shall allow users to reuse schemas.
The service shall allow users to exchange XML data without binding them to a specific database implementation.
The first release shall support a pilot set of systems publishing approved XML assets through the service.
The first release shall support a pilot set of systems consuming approved XML assets through the service.
The first release shall reduce custom point-to-point work for the pilot set of systems.
Shared definitions shall remain consistent across users of the service.
The system shall accept an XML document only when it conforms to the approved schema and uses the managed terms and structures exactly as defined for that version.
The system shall reject an XML document if required elements are missing.
The system shall reject an XML document if values are out of range.
The system shall reject an XML document if values are of the wrong type.
The system shall reject an XML document if it references an outdated definition.
The system shall reject an XML document if it references an unsupported definition.
When source data does not conform, the service shall return clear validation errors.
When source data does not conform, the service shall keep the document out of the approved store until the issuer corrects it.
The service shall block a nonconforming document from being treated as valid.
If a replacement exists for a retired asset, the system shall warn users and redirect them to the newer approved asset.
The service shall provide enough metadata to make the correct asset choice obvious.
The service shall include the asset's purpose in its metadata.
The service shall include any known replacement or dependency in the asset's metadata.
The service shall provide guided selection.
The service shall explain why the approved current version is the recommended one.
The service shall provide plain-language descriptions for onboarding.
The service shall provide sample payloads for onboarding.
The service shall provide validation feedback that tells a new integrator what they did wrong and how to fix it.
Approved artifacts shall show full current metadata and usage notes.
Approved artifacts shall show sample payloads that match the active schema exactly.
The system shall hide or minimize information that could confuse a new user, such as obsolete examples or unsupported fields, unless the information is needed for migration or audit purposes.
If the content is sensitive or controlled, discovery of alternate versions shall be limited so that only authorized roles can see that the alternate version exists at all.
The system’s practical rule for handling an item shall be based on whether the item is needed beyond the source system and whether it can be exposed without violating policy or mission need.
The system shall audit log any change to a managed definition, schema, term set, or document.
The audit log shall record who performed the change, when it occurred, what changed, and which version was affected.
The system shall log access events for sensitive items.
The system shall log approvals.
The system shall log rejections.
The system shall log retirements.
The system shall log permission changes.
The system shall log bulk or system-generated activity at a summarized level with enough detail to reconstruct what happened without flooding the audit store.
The only exception to audit logging shall be routine background processing that never changes managed content and does not touch sensitive data.
A non-authoritative version may be selectable for formal use only in rare cases when the authoritative version is unavailable, not yet published, or explicitly exempted for a specific mission need.
An exception allowing selection of a non-authoritative version must require an approved waiver or designated authority sign-off.
The system must record the justification for the exception.
The system must record the scope of the exception.
The system must record the expiration of the exception.
